statement: a fundamental Bell-state fidelity ceiling of 0.9787; 189 measurements, none above
label: REFUTED
reason: 1 - phi^-8 = 0.978701 bounds Bell-state preparation fidelity, which is distinct from RB two-qubit gate fidelity. Comparing strictly like-for-like Bell-state preparation experiments (population + parity oscillation tomography), Benhelm et al. (Nat. Phys. 4, 463, 2008) measured raw Bell-state fidelity F_Bell = 0.993(1) without SPAM subtraction (14.3 sigma above 0.9787); Gaebler et al. (PRL 117, 060505, 2016) measured 0.9955(5) raw (0.9991(4) SPAM-corrected); Clark et al. (PRL 127, 130505, 2021) measured 0.9994(3) raw; and Ding et al. (PRX 13, 031035, 2023) exceeded 0.985 raw on superconducting fluxonium. Furthermore, 0/189 IBM runs (max F_Bell = 0.9773) never reached the 0.9787 regime and had zero statistical power to test a ceiling.

evidence_audit.verification_domain: mathematical_and_published_hardware_falsification (like-for-like Bell-state preparation fidelity, distinct from RB gate fidelity)
evidence_audit.remaining_limitations: 0/189 IBM runs had max Bell fidelity 0.9773 and therefore had zero statistical power to test a 0.9787 ceiling.

gate_vs_state_distinction: Randomized benchmarking (RB) average 2-qubit gate fidelity (e.g. Kandala et al. 2021 0.9977(2) CNOT; Ballance et al. 2016 RB gate metric) isolates single-gate error from state preparation and measurement (SPAM) and is NOT interchangeable with Bell-state preparation fidelity. Falsification of F_max = 1 - phi^-8 = 0.978701 must use like-for-like Bell-state preparation + tomography measurements.
